hints: A negative cycle can be anywhere in the graph, not only reachable from one chosen source.
Initialize every distance to zero, which is equivalent to adding a zero-cost super-source to all vertices.
After n relaxation rounds, a vertex changed on the nth round lies on or is affected by a negative cycle; follow parents enough times to enter it.
analogy: Give every vertex a free starting point, then repeatedly improve routes; endless improvement reveals a negative loop.
example: A cycle with total weight -2 keeps lowering the route cost every time it is repeated.
algorithm: Bellman-Ford over all edges with dist=0. If no update on the nth round, print NO; otherwise follow parent n times from the last updated vertex, then collect parent links until returning to the same vertex and output the cycle.
correctness: Without a negative cycle, shortest simple paths use at most n-1 edges, so no improvement can remain on round n; following parents enters a cycle whose total weight is negative.
